summary: Contestants demonstrate their knowledge and application of C++ programming by completing programming tasks using structured design, algorithm development, and object-oriented methodologies. The event is conducted on the Windows operating system, and contestants must bring their own equipment and reference materials. All work is completed on-site and uploaded electronically.
time_limits: No more than ten (10) minutes orientation
No more than ninety (90) minutes testing time
No more than ten (10) minutes wrap-up
submission_requirements: All student-produced jobs completed on-site are uploaded electronically and are not printed at the national level
what_to_bring: Published and/or unpublished non-electronic written reference materials
Computer or laptop/notebook (USB-Type A or adapter required)
A full-size keyboard may be used (no printer is needed)
Contestant must use one of these IDEs: Visual Studio 2022, Visual Studio Code, VSCode, DevC++ with Ming compiler, Code:Blocks
Only pre-written code that is hard copied is allowed
competencies: Demonstrate foundational understanding of computer science principles and proficiency in C++ syntax, semantics, and standard libraries to solve programming challenges

Design, develop, test, and maintain interactive C++ applications using modern programming practices, including control flow, logical operations, classes, file access, I/O operations, loops, methods, arrays, and advanced data structures
Implement efficient algorithms and utilize structured and object-oriented design techniques to create scalable and maintainable C++ software solutions
Create and interpret UML diagrams to model software architecture and communicate design decisions in C++ projects
Apply modern C++ standards to write safer, more efficient, and more expressive code using updated language features, best practices, and standard conventions
Use pointers to manage memory safely, prevent leaks, and ensure reliable resource handling in C++ applications
Utilize debugging tools within modern C++ toolchains to identify logic errors, inspect runtime behavior, and optimize program performance
Leverage the expanded C++ Standard Library (STL), including advanced containers, algorithms, and utilities, to write more efficient and maintainable software
judging_notes: Carry-in and setup of equipment must be done solely by the contestant within the time allotted
Business Professionals of America assumes no responsibility for hardware/software provided by the contestant
No equipment, supplies or materials other than those specified for the event will be allowed in the testing area
Previous Business Professionals of America tests and/or sample tests (handwritten, photocopied or keyed) may not be taken into the testing area. Violation of this rule will result in disqualification
eligibility_notes: Any secondary or postsecondary division contestant may enter this application event
